result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.dag_longest_path()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the longest path in a directed acyclic graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L45421-L45483){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.dag_longest_path() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![DAG longest path](/assets/graphs/dag-longest-path.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A seven-node DAG whose edges carry task durations. The heaviest chain of tasks, the critical path B, D, F, G, is drawn in the accent color: its durations 3 + 4 + 2 add up to 9.0, more than any other route from a source to G." width="100%"} In a DAG of tasks and dependencies, the longest path is the *critical path*: the chain of tasks that determines the earliest possible finish time, so that any delay along it delays the whole project. On an unweighted graph its length is the number of edges; on a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) it is the total edge weight, so weights can carry task durations. Edges without a weight count as `1.0`, and of several parallel edges the heaviest counts. Unlike shortest paths, longest paths are only well defined without cycles, so the graph must be a DAG. The length is available from `dag_longest_path_length()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The node IDs along a longest path, in order. When several paths tie, the one ending at (and then extending from) the lowest node ID is returned. An empty graph gives an empty list; a graph without edges gives a single node. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or contains a cycle. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} With task durations as weights, the critical path runs through the slow test suite, even though the documentation branch starts with the longer first task: ::: {#730fc2ab .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True) .add_nodes(["fetch", "compile", "test", "package", "docs", "publish"]) .add_edges([ ("fetch", "compile", 3.0), ("compile", "test", 10.0), ("test", "package", 2.0), ("fetch", "docs", 4.0), ("docs", "publish", 1.0), ]) ) [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in graph.dag_longest_path()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['fetch', 'compile', 'test', 'package'] ``` ::: :::
